meta.description: Countries classified by role in the corridor war. Based on official doctrines, stated goals, and observed behavior.

tiers.principal: Sets the global agenda. Builds or blocks corridors. Has independent military, economic, and diplomatic capacity to act alone.
tiers.regional_power: Shapes its region. Can swing between principals. Has enough weight to block or enable corridors in its geography.
tiers.satellite: Aligned with a principal or regional power. Limited independent action but strategically located.
tiers.contested: Territory multiple powers compete over. Alignment unstable or fractured.
tiers.swing_state: Courted by both sides. Has leverage because both blocs need it. Plays principals against each other.

principals.name: United States
official_doctrine: 2022 National Security Strategy: 'Out-compete China, constrain Russia, shape rules of the road'
2025 National Security Strategy (Trump): 'Donroe Doctrine — deny non-hemispheric competitors the Western Hemisphere'
IMEC co-architect: counter-BRI corridor through India-Gulf-Israel-Europe
AUKUS/Quad: military-diplomatic architecture to contain China in Indo-Pacific
Maximum pressure on Iran: sanctions, strikes, Hormuz control
goals: Maintain dollar as global reserve currency
Keep chokepoints open and under allied control (Hormuz, Suez, Panama, Malacca)
Prevent China from dominating Eurasian trade routes
Secure semiconductor supply chain (Taiwan/TSMC)
Neutralize Iran as corridor blocker
Expel China/Russia from Western Hemisphere
tools: Alliance network (NATO, Quad, AUKUS, Abraham Accords)

principals.name: China
official_doctrine: Belt and Road Initiative (2013): 'Community of shared future for mankind' — infrastructure connectivity across 150+ countries
Made in China 2025: tech self-sufficiency in 10 strategic sectors
Dual Circulation Strategy (2020): reduce dependence on Western markets
Global Security Initiative (2022): alternative to US-led security architecture
Global Development Initiative (2021): counter-narrative to Western development model
goals: Secure overland trade routes to Europe bypassing US-controlled seas
Control critical mineral supply chains (lithium, cobalt, rare earths)
Establish yuan as alternative reserve currency
Reunify Taiwan (seize semiconductor chokepoint)
Build Indian Ocean port network (String of Pearls)
Make BRI the default global infrastructure standard
vulnerabilities: Malacca Strait dependency (80% of oil imports)

principals.name: Russia
official_doctrine: 2023 Foreign Policy Concept: 'Multipolar world order, end Western hegemony'
Near Abroad doctrine: former Soviet states are Russia's sphere of influence
Energy as weapon: pipeline politics (Nord Stream, TurkStream, Power of Siberia)
Arctic Strategy: Northern Sea Route as alternative global corridor
goals: Prevent NATO expansion (Ukraine as red line)
Maintain energy leverage over Europe
Control Arctic shipping route as ice melts
Secure warm-water naval bases (Tartus lost, Crimea contested)
Capture African mineral belt via Wagner/Africa Corps
Keep INSTC alive as Russia-India-Iran corridor

principals.name: India
official_doctrine: Multi-alignment / Strategic Autonomy: maintains ties with US, Russia, and Gulf simultaneously
Neighborhood First: prevent Chinese encirclement in Indian Ocean
Act East Policy: deepen ASEAN and Pacific engagement
Make in India: become global manufacturing alternative to China
SAGAR (Security and Growth for All in the Region): Indian Ocean leadership
goals: Become IMEC's eastern anchor (replace China as global factory)
Secure Indian Ocean from Chinese String of Pearls
Counter CPEC/Gwadar with Chabahar/INSTC
Achieve semiconductor manufacturing capability
Maintain strategic autonomy (buy Russian oil AND join Quad)
Neutralize Pakistan as China's proxy

regional_powers.name: Turkey
official_doctrine: Blue Homeland (Mavi Vatan): Turkish maritime sovereignty over Eastern Mediterranean and Black Sea
Neo-Ottoman reach: influence from Balkans to Central Asia to Horn of Africa
NATO member that buys Russian S-400s and invades Syria
goals: Control Eastern Mediterranean energy routes
Build Turkic corridor (Turkey → Azerbaijan → Central Asia)
Become indispensable to ALL corridors (IMEC, BRI, Middle Corridor all need Turkish geography)
Dominate post-Assad Syria
Expand defense exports (TB2 drones as diplomatic tool)
regional_powers.leans_toward: Both — NATO member but acts independently. Blocks Sweden's NATO bid, buys Russian S-400, invades Syria, backs Azerbaijan. Erdogan plays every side.

regional_powers.name: Iran
official_doctrine: Forward Defense: use proxy network to fight enemies far from Iranian soil
Axis of Resistance: Hamas, Hezbollah, Houthis, Iraqi militias, Syrian loyalists
Neither East nor West (rhetoric) — but now firmly in China-Russia axis
Nuclear ambiguity: 60% enrichment, weeks from breakout
goals: Survive regime change attempts
Control chokepoints (Hormuz, Bab al-Mandab via Houthis)
Block IMEC (requires Saudi-Israel normalization Iran opposes)
Maintain land bridge to Mediterranean (Tehran → Baghdad → Damascus → Beirut) — NOW SEVERED
Achieve nuclear deterrent
regional_powers.leans_toward: BLOCKER axis (China 25yr deal, Russia 20yr treaty). But proxies are collapsing: Hezbollah decapitated, Assad fallen, land bridge cut.

regional_powers.name: Saudi Arabia
official_doctrine: Vision 2030: economic diversification away from oil dependency
IMEC signatory: committed to India-Gulf-Europe corridor
BRICS member (2024): hedging toward multipolar order
Accepting yuan for some oil sales: gradual petrodollar diversification
goals: Diversify economy before oil era ends (NEOM, entertainment, tourism, tech)
Normalize with Israel (paused after Oct 7, still strategic goal)
Become IMEC's Gulf anchor
Maintain US security umbrella while hedging with China
Contain Iran (but also signed China-brokered deal with Iran)
Control Yemen outcome
regional_powers.leans_toward: BUILDER but hedging heavily. Joined BRICS, accepts yuan, buys Chinese weapons — but core security still depends on US.

regional_powers.name: United Arab Emirates
official_doctrine: Economic hedging: invest everywhere, align with no one exclusively
Abraham Accords signatory: normalized with Israel
Port empire: DP World operates 78 terminals in 40+ countries
AI/tech pivot: attracting Western tech firms and talent
goals: Build the Gulf's dominant port/logistics network
Control Red Sea access points (Berbera, Assab, Bosaso, Socotra)
Maintain relationships with US, China, Israel, India simultaneously
Win Horn of Africa proxy competition vs Turkey and Saudi
Become AI/fintech hub
regional_powers.leans_toward: BUILDER-leaning but the ultimate hedger. Hosts Chinese military tech, Indian IMEC infrastructure, US military bases, and Israeli intelligence all at the same time.

regional_powers.name: Israel
official_doctrine: Abraham Accords: normalize with Arab states, isolate Iran
IMEC critical node: Mediterranean endpoint of the corridor
Qualitative Military Edge (QME): maintain tech superiority in region
Iran as existential threat: prevention doctrine
goals: Eliminate Iranian nuclear threat
Expand Abraham Accords (Saudi normalization = strategic prize)
Become IMEC's indispensable corridor node (Haifa port)
Destroy remaining Iranian proxy network
Secure recognition from more states (Somaliland)
regional_powers.leans_toward: BUILDER core. But Haifa port has Chinese operator (SIPG), creating a vulnerability. Post-Oct 7 war complicates IMEC timeline.

regional_powers.name: Pakistan
official_doctrine: Strategic depth: use Afghanistan as buffer against India
All-weather friendship with China: CPEC as economic lifeline
Nuclear deterrence against India
Kashmir as core issue
goals: Survive economically (IMF bailouts, Chinese debt)
Operationalize CPEC/Gwadar as Chinese Indian Ocean access
Counter India's rise as regional hegemon
Maintain nuclear parity with India
Control Taliban enough to prevent blowback
regional_powers.leans_toward: BLOCKER — China's primary South Asian partner. CPEC makes Pakistan economically dependent on Beijing. But military still receives some US equipment.

regional_powers.name: Egypt
official_doctrine: Suez Canal controller: 12% of world trade, $9.4B annual revenue
Military-first governance: army controls 25-40% of GDP
Balance US military aid ($1.3B/year) with diversifying to Russian/Chinese weapons
goals: Protect Suez Canal revenue (IMEC could reduce Suez traffic if overland route works)
Prevent Ethiopia's GERD dam from controlling Nile flow
Stabilize Libya's eastern border
Prevent Sudan's RSF from winning (security threat on southern border)
Maintain US military aid while buying Russian jets
regional_powers.leans_toward: SWING — Suez gives Egypt leverage over ALL corridor plans. Egypt benefits from corridor competition as long as traffic keeps flowing through Suez.

regional_powers.name: Japan
official_doctrine: Free and Open Indo-Pacific (FOIP): Japan's counter-BRI framework since 2016
Quad member: coordinate with US, India, Australia against China
Constitutional reinterpretation (2015): collective self-defense now permitted
2022 National Security Strategy: largest military buildup since WWII ($320B over 5 years)
goals: Prevent Chinese domination of East/South China Sea
Secure Taiwan Strait (90% of Japan's oil passes through)
Build alternative infrastructure in Southeast Asia and India (counter-BRI)
Maintain US alliance as security backbone
Develop semiconductor independence (TSMC fab in Kumamoto)
regional_powers.leans_toward: BUILDER core. Japan invested $65B+ in Indo-Pacific infrastructure to counter BRI before the US even woke up to it.

regional_powers.name: Australia
official_doctrine: AUKUS: nuclear submarines to patrol Indo-Pacific
Quad member
Five Eyes intelligence sharing
Pacific Step-Up: counter Chinese influence in Pacific Islands
goals: Prevent Chinese military base in Pacific Islands (Solomon Islands pact = red line)
Secure critical mineral exports (lithium, iron ore, LNG)
Maintain US alliance as ultimate security guarantee
Counter Chinese economic coercion (2020 trade war with China)
regional_powers.leans_toward: BUILDER core. AUKUS is the strongest commitment any US ally has made to the counter-China architecture.

regional_powers.name: France
official_doctrine: Strategic autonomy: European defense independent of US
Indo-Pacific power (territories in Pacific, Indian Ocean, Caribbean)
Françafrique: declining but persistent influence in West/Central Africa
goals: Maintain Mediterranean/African influence (being expelled by Wagner)
Protect French Pacific territories (New Caledonia, Polynesia)
Lead EU defense integration
Secure energy transition minerals from former colonies
regional_powers.leans_toward: BUILDER but angry about AUKUS (lost $66B sub deal). Acts independently from US. Being replaced by Russia/Wagner across Sahel.

regional_powers.name: North Korea
official_doctrine: Nuclear deterrence: survival through escalation threat
Byungjin: parallel development of nuclear weapons and economy
Self-reliance (juche) — in practice, depends on China and Russia
goals: Regime survival above all else
Nuclear ICBM capability targeting US mainland
Sanctions evasion (crypto theft, arms sales, forced labor exports)
Troops-for-tech deal with Russia (soldiers in Ukraine for missile/satellite tech)
regional_powers.leans_toward: BLOCKER. Provides Russia with artillery shells and soldiers for Ukraine. Receives satellite and nuclear submarine tech in return. China is economic lifeline.

swing_states.name: Singapore
swing_states.leverage: Controls Strait of Malacca chokepoint. $1.27T in sovereign capital. Hosts US military logistics AND Chinese investment. If forced to choose, global shipping reroutes.
swing_states.plays_both: US military uses Changi Naval Base. China is largest trading partner. PSA ports operate globally. Both sides need Singapore neutral.

swing_states.name: Vietnam
swing_states.leverage: Largest beneficiary of China decoupling — manufacturing moving from China to Vietnam. South China Sea claimant (anti-China). But communist party maintains party-to-party ties with CPC.
swing_states.plays_both: Samsung's largest factory complex globally. US upgraded to Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (2023). Russia is traditional arms supplier. China is largest trading partner AND territorial adversary.

swing_states.name: Kazakhstan
swing_states.leverage: Middle Corridor (Trans-Caspian) runs through Kazakhstan — the Russia-bypass route connecting China to Europe. Massive oil/gas reserves. Uranium supplier (40% of global production). Joined Abraham Accords (2025).
swing_states.plays_both: China's BRI overland corridor depends on Kazakhstan. Russia considers it 'near abroad.' US and EU court it for Middle Corridor. Joined BRICS but also signed Abraham Accords.

swing_states.name: Indonesia
swing_states.leverage: World's largest Muslim-majority country (280M). Controls Malacca/Sunda/Lombok straits. Massive nickel reserves (critical for EV batteries). ASEAN's largest economy.
swing_states.plays_both: China's largest BRI recipient in SE Asia. US wants Indonesia in counter-China architecture. Indonesia refuses to choose — 'a million friends, zero enemies' doctrine.

swing_states.name: Brazil
swing_states.leverage: Largest Latin American economy. BRICS founding member. Amazon rainforest gives climate leverage. Major food exporter to China.
swing_states.plays_both: BRICS member but also US ally on most trade issues. Lula balances Washington and Beijing. China is largest trading partner. US is largest foreign investor.

swing_states.name: South Africa
swing_states.leverage: Cape of Good Hope route gains importance when Suez/Red Sea disrupted. BRICS host (2023 expansion summit). Critical minerals (platinum, manganese, chrome).
swing_states.plays_both: Hosted BRICS expansion. ICC member that issued Putin arrest warrant. US ally on trade. China's biggest African trading partner.

swing_states.name: Mexico
swing_states.leverage: Nearshoring boom — manufacturing relocating from China to Mexico. US's largest trading partner. USMCA member. Border = leverage over US immigration policy.
swing_states.plays_both: Economically tied to US (80% of exports). But Chinese investment surging. Fentanyl precursor pipeline from China through Mexico. Caught between Donroe Doctrine pressure and Chinese manufacturing investment.

swing_states.name: Georgia
swing_states.leverage: Middle Corridor transit state — BTC pipeline, South Caucasus Pipeline, and rail link to Turkey all cross Georgia. Only Caucasus route that bypasses both Russia and Iran.
swing_states.plays_both: EU candidate status (2023). But ruling party (Georgian Dream) tilting toward Russia. Massive protests over 'foreign agents' law. Strategic location makes both sides compete for it.

us_satellites.name: Bahrain
us_satellites.role: US Fifth Fleet headquarters. Abraham Accords signatory. Saudi dependent.

us_satellites.name: Jordan
us_satellites.role: IMEC overland transit state (Israel → Jordan → Saudi). Hosts US military bases. Survives on Gulf subsidies. Critical corridor node.

us_satellites.name: South Korea
us_satellites.role: Samsung/SK Hynix = semiconductor power. 28,500 US troops stationed. THAAD deployment. Indo-Pacific tech corridor node.

us_satellites.name: Philippines
us_satellites.role: First island chain anchor. 9 EDCA bases for US forces. South China Sea frontline state. Marcos Jr. reversed Duterte's China tilt.

us_satellites.name: Taiwan
us_satellites.role: TSMC produces 90% of advanced chips. THE critical node of global tech supply chain. US committed to defend under Taiwan Relations Act. China's #1 target.

us_satellites.name: Poland
us_satellites.role: NATO's eastern anchor. Largest European military buildup ($35B+ spending). Absorbs Ukraine defense logistics. Key node if Northern Corridor reopens post-Russia.

us_satellites.name: Greece
us_satellites.role: Piraeus port was sold to COSCO (China) in 2016 — Mediterranean endpoint of BRI maritime route. Now US pressuring to limit Chinese operations. NATO naval base at Souda Bay.

us_satellites.name: Morocco
us_satellites.role: Abraham Accords signatory (in exchange for US recognition of Western Sahara). Guards Strait of Gibraltar — the Atlantic-Mediterranean chokepoint. Tanger Med port is Africa's largest.

us_satellites.name: United Kingdom
us_satellites.role: AUKUS co-architect. Five Eyes. London as global financial hub. Diego Garcia (Indian Ocean base). Gibraltar (Mediterranean chokepoint). Post-Brexit, locked into US orbit.

us_satellites.name: Germany
us_satellites.role: Europe's largest economy but energy-dependent (lost Russian gas, now buys US LNG). Ramstein Air Base = US European command hub. Deindustrializing post-Nord Stream. IMEC's European financial anchor.

china_satellites.name: Myanmar
china_satellites.role: CMEC corridor state. Kyaukpyu port = China's Malacca bypass. Junta depends on Chinese UN veto. Shwe gas pipeline feeds Kunming.

china_satellites.name: Cambodia
china_satellites.role: Ream Naval Base — suspected Chinese military facility 300km from Vietnam. BRI infrastructure recipient. Hun family dynasty depends on Chinese patronage.

china_satellites.name: Laos
china_satellites.role: China-Laos Railway (2021) — first BRI rail connection into SE Asia. Debt-to-GDP over 80%, mostly owed to China. Landlocked, entirely dependent.

china_satellites.name: Sri Lanka
china_satellites.role: Hambantota port — 99-year Chinese lease. Indian Ocean surveillance position. 2022 economic collapse partly from Chinese debt. India and China now compete for influence.

china_satellites.name: Djibouti
china_satellites.patron: Multi (US, China, France, Japan all have bases)
china_satellites.role: Guards Bab al-Mandab strait. China's first overseas military base (2017). US Camp Lemonnier. France's largest African base. 4 foreign militaries in one tiny country.

china_satellites.name: Solomon Islands
china_satellites.role: 2022 security pact allows Chinese naval visits. Breaches Pacific island chain. Australia's red line.

china_satellites.name: Eritrea
china_satellites.role: Assab port (UAE operated). Red Sea coastline. Sent troops into Tigray. 'North Korea of Africa' — isolated, strategic.

russia_satellites.name: Belarus
russia_satellites.role: Staging ground for Ukraine invasion. Russian nuclear weapons deployed. Lukashenko entirely dependent on Putin. Northern Corridor transit state.

russia_satellites.name: Syria (pre-2024)
russia_satellites.role: WAS: Russia's Mediterranean naval base (Tartus), Iran's land bridge to Hezbollah. Assad fell Dec 2024 — both lost everything.

russia_satellites.name: Cuba
russia_satellites.role: Russian intelligence facilities 90 miles from Florida. Chinese signals intercept station (Lourdes). Venezuela's oil lifeline. Donroe Doctrine target.

russia_satellites.name: Nicaragua
russia_satellites.role: Hosts Russian military equipment. China considered a Nicaragua canal (alternative to Panama). Ortega regime entirely depends on external patrons.

russia_satellites.name: Mali
russia_satellites.role: Expelled French forces 2022. Wagner controls gold mines. Russia's Sahel anchor state. Uranium access.

russia_satellites.name: Central African Republic
russia_satellites.role: First Wagner deployment in Africa (2018). Diamond and gold concessions. Wagner provides presidential guard.

russia_satellites.name: Burkina Faso
russia_satellites.role: Coup government expelled France (2023). Wagner invited. Alliance of Sahel States with Mali and Niger. Manganese and gold.

iran_satellites.name: Yemen (Houthi-controlled)
iran_satellites.role: Controls Bab al-Mandab approach. Red Sea blockade force. 130+ attacks on shipping since Oct 2023. Iran's most effective remaining proxy.

iran_satellites.name: Iraq (Shia militias / PMF)
iran_satellites.role: Popular Mobilization Forces integrated into Iraqi state but loyal to Tehran. Control border crossings. Iran's land corridor to Syria (before Assad fell).

iran_satellites.name: Lebanon (Hezbollah)
iran_satellites.role: WAS Iran's most powerful proxy. Nasrallah killed Sep 2024. Command structure decapitated. Still holds 100K+ rockets but operationally degraded.

iran_satellites.name: Venezuela
iran_satellites.role: Largest proven oil reserves. Hezbollah financial networks. Russian military presence. Chinese debt ($10B+). Maduro seized Jan 2026 (speculative). Triple-patron state.

contested_zones.name: Ukraine
contested_zones.corridor_impact: Northern Corridor (China-Europe via Russia) destroyed. EU energy dependence on Russia broken. Russia depleted militarily.

contested_zones.name: Syria (post-Assad)
contested_zones.status: HTS-controlled, fragmented. Turkey dominant in north. Kurds hold east. Reconstruction needed.
contested_zones.corridor_impact: Iran's land bridge severed. Russia lost Tartus. Potential Abraham Accords expansion. Could become IMEC overland route if stabilized.

contested_zones.name: Sudan
contested_zones.status: Civil war since Apr 2023. RSF vs SAF. World's largest displacement crisis.
contested_zones.corridor_impact: Port Sudan is Red Sea prize. Western shore of Red Sea ungovernable. Blocks any stable Horn of Africa corridor architecture.

contested_zones.name: Libya
contested_zones.corridor_impact: Mediterranean south shore. Oil exports. Migration leverage over EU. Turkey's EEZ deal blocks EastMed pipeline.

contested_zones.name: Somalia
contested_zones.status: Fragmented. Federal govt vs Al-Shabaab vs Somaliland vs Puntland.
contested_zones.corridor_impact: Indian Ocean coastline. Overlooking Gulf of Aden shipping. Somaliland's Berbera = Bab al-Mandab flanking position.

contested_zones.name: Afghanistan
contested_zones.status: Taliban-controlled since Aug 2021. No international recognition. $1-3T mineral wealth untapped.
contested_zones.corridor_impact: Crossroads of CPEC, INSTC, and Central Asian corridor. Mineral wealth (lithium, rare earths) coveted by China. Instability blocks all transit.

contested_zones.name: Ethiopia
contested_zones.status: Post-Tigray ceasefire (Nov 2022). Amhara/Oromia tensions ongoing. GERD dam dispute with Egypt.
contested_zones.corridor_impact: Horn's largest economy. 95% of Djibouti port traffic is Ethiopian. If Ethiopia fragments, Djibouti loses purpose and China's base loses rationale.

contested_zones.name: Greenland
contested_zones.status: Danish territory. Trump demands purchase/control. JD Vance visits. Independence movement growing.
contested_by: China (rare earth mining interest, shut down 2021)
contested_zones.corridor_impact: Arctic corridor anchor. Rare earth deposits. Thule Space Base. Melting ice opening Northern Sea Route — Greenland controls the Atlantic entrance.

alliances.name: Builder Core Alliance
alliances.goal: Build alternative corridors to BRI. Keep chokepoints open. Maintain dollar system.

alliances.name: Blocker Axis
alliances.goal: Block Western corridors. Build alternative payment systems. Control chokepoints. Prevent US-led order.

alliances.name: BRICS+
alliances.goal: De-dollarize. Create alternative financial architecture. Multipolar order. NOTE: India, Saudi, UAE are in BOTH Builder and BRICS — that's the hedging.

alliances.name: Alliance of Sahel States
alliances.goal: Expel Western military presence. Russian security partnership. Control gold and uranium exports.
